title: Deep Seabed Mining: Revisions to Regulations for Exploration License and Commercial Recovery Permit Applications (final rule)
date_evidence: Federal Register :: Deep Seabed Mining: Revisions to Regulations for Exploration License and Commercial Recovery Permit Applications ... documents/2026/01/21/2026-01044 ... On January 21, 2026, NOAA issued the final rule consolidating and accelerating its permitting process for deep seabed mining under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act
key_claim: On 21 January 2026 NOAA issued a final rule revising and accelerating its regulations for exploration licences and commercial recovery permits under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act (DSHMRA), the domestic legal instrument that lets the United States authorise deep-seabed mining in international waters outside the UN's International Seabed Authority process.
frame_summary: Argues, as a regulatory instrument, that the United States can and will permit deep-seabed mining under its own domestic law, establishing a national track that operates outside the multilateral ISA/UNCLOS framework.
notes: Tier 1 structural anchor (21 Jan 2026, ~5 months): the canonical US instrument enabling unilateral seabed permitting. One anchor permitted.

title: The Council of the International Seabed Authority advanced negotiations on the Mining Code
date_evidence: The Council of the International Seabed Authority concluded Part I of its 31st session on 19 March 2026 in Kingston, Jamaica ... The Council is expected to reconvene in July 2026 for the second part of its 31st session ... to continue advancing negotiations on the Mining Code
key_claim: The ISA Council concluded Part I of its 31st session on 19 March 2026 in Kingston without adopting the long-delayed Mining Code or approving any commercial exploitation, leaving environmental safeguards, liability, inspection, compliance and benefit-sharing unresolved, and is due to reconvene in July 2026 to continue negotiations.
frame_summary: Argues, as the multilateral authority, that exploitation in the international seabed Area remains un-permitted because the Mining Code is unfinished and contested, so no lawful commercial mining can yet proceed under UNCLOS.
notes: Tier 1; the multilateral track that the US route bypasses - still without a Mining Code as of March 2026.

title: Critical minerals: The US bid to bypass international rules on deep sea mining
date_evidence: Critical minerals: The US bid to bypass international rules on deep sea mining ... published on the Lowy Institute's Interpreter on 22 May 2026 ... the US argues it neither signed nor ratified UNCLOS ... even China has denounced the move, positioning itself as a champion of multilateralism
key_claim: A 22 May 2026 Lowy Institute analysis argues the US bid to permit deep-sea mining under its own law bypasses the ISA and the UNCLOS principle of the seabed as the common heritage of humankind; the US contends it never ratified UNCLOS and so is not bound by the ISA process, while the ISA Secretary-General insists no state may unilaterally exploit Area resources, and even China has denounced the move while positioning itself as a defender of multilateralism.
frame_summary: Argues that the US unilateral seabed-mining bid is a geopolitical gamble that undermines the rules-based ocean order and cedes the multilateralist high ground to China.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank; the geopolitics of bypassing the ISA and the China-positioning point.

title: 1st Part of the 31st Annual Session of the International Seabed Authority (ISA) Council
date_evidence: 1st Part of the 31st Annual Session of the International Seabed Authority (ISA) Council ... 9-19 March 2026 ... Kingston, Jamaica ... two weeks of negotiations concluded with no Mining Code adopted; France, Costa Rica, the Africa Group, Mexico, Germany, Palau and Brazil raised scientific, environmental and governance gaps
key_claim: IISD's Earth Negotiations Bulletin record of the ISA Council's 9-19 March 2026 session documents that negotiations ended with no Mining Code, with France, Costa Rica, the Africa Group, Mexico, Germany, Palau and Brazil among states stressing that scientific, environmental and governance gaps must be resolved before any mining is considered.
frame_summary: Argues, as a neutral negotiations record, that a substantial bloc of states is actively blocking a rushed Mining Code, so the multilateral route to seabed mining remains stalled by genuine unresolved disputes.
notes: Tier 2 institutional negotiations record; corroborates the multilateral stalemate and names the blocking states.

title: No code, no permits: ISA deep-sea mining talks end in stalemate
date_evidence: No code, no permits: ISA deep-sea mining talks end in stalemate ... published by Oceanographic Magazine on March 20, 2026 ... ISA talks ended with no mining approved and no Mining Code adopted, as 40 nations unite for a deep-sea moratorium
key_claim: Oceanographic Magazine (20 March 2026) reports that the ISA talks closed with no mining approved and no Mining Code, while around 40 countries now back a moratorium or precautionary pause on deep-sea mining, including France (which has legislated a ban), the UK, Germany, Canada, New Zealand and numerous Pacific Island states.
frame_summary: Argues that the international community is hardening against deep-sea mining, with a 40-country moratorium bloc forming even as the US track advances, deepening the governance split.
notes: Tier 3; the 40-country moratorium bloc - core of the governance-fracture and counter-argument.

title: US Deep-Sea Mining Policy Is Eroding Its Pacific Partnerships
date_evidence: US Deep-Sea Mining Policy Is Eroding Its Pacific Partnerships - The Diplomat (thediplomat.com/2026/05/, May 2026) ... the unilateral approach strains relations with Pacific Island states that favour the ISA process and a precautionary pause
key_claim: A May 2026 analysis in The Diplomat argues that the unilateral US deep-sea mining approach is straining Washington's relationships with Pacific Island states, many of which favour the ISA process and a precautionary pause, undercutting US influence in a region central to its strategic competition with China.
frame_summary: Argues that the unilateral seabed-mining push carries a concrete alliance cost, alienating Pacific partners the US needs for its wider Indo-Pacific strategy.
notes: Tier 3; the alliance / Indo-Pacific cost of the unilateral track.

title: Flagship deep-sea mining project financially unviable, report says
date_evidence: Flagship deep-sea mining project financially unviable, report says ... March 2026 ... an independent analysis commissioned by Deep Sea Mining Campaign, Greenpeace International and MiningWatch Canada concluded the project would fail to generate meaningful profit ... the company's own Pre-Feasibility Study showed reserves sustaining just eight years of operation and generating zero profit, with 113.1 million wet metric tonnes of speculative resources added to its estimates
key_claim: A March 2026 report covered by Oceanographic Magazine - an independent analysis commissioned by the Deep Sea Mining Campaign, Greenpeace International and MiningWatch Canada - concluded that the flagship Pacific nodule project would fail to generate meaningful profit, noting the developer's own Pre-Feasibility Study implied reserves for only about eight years of operation and zero profit, with 113.1 million wet metric tonnes of speculative resources folded into its economics.
frame_summary: Argues that the economics of flagship deep-sea nodule mining do not yet work, so the new supply frontier may be commercially marginal regardless of the permitting fast track.
notes: Tier 3 (advocacy-commissioned analysis, treat directionally); the commercial-viability counter-argument.

title: NOAA Determines TMC USA's Consolidated Deep-Seabed Mining Application is in Full Compliance
date_evidence: NOAA Determines TMC USA's Consolidated Deep-Seabed Mining Application is in Full Compliance ... news-release/2026/05/01 ... covers a ~65,000 km2 exploration and commercial recovery area in the Clarion Clipperton Zone ... estimated resource of 619 million tonnes of wet nodules ... expects a permit before the end of Q1 2027
key_claim: On 1 May 2026 The Metals Company announced that NOAA had ruled its consolidated US application for a Clarion-Clipperton Zone exploration licence and commercial recovery permit to be in full compliance; the application covers about 65,000 km2 and an estimated 619 million tonnes of wet polymetallic nodules (nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese), with the company expecting a permit before the end of Q1 2027.
frame_summary: Argues, from the developer's side, that the US commercial track is real and advancing, with a permit and first production imminent on a defined timeline.
notes: Tier 4 company source (treat directionally); evidence the commercial track is reaching full compliance, with figures and timeline.
